name: Air India
description: India's flag carrier, connecting Indian cities with destinations across the world.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A350, Boeing 787 Dreamliner and Boeing 777 aircraft.
destinations: Domestic destinations across India and international destinations in Asia, Europe, North America and other regions. Routes may change.
history: Founded in 1932 as Tata Airlines by J. R. D. Tata. It later became Air India and returned to the Tata Group in 2022.
services: Domestic and international flights, cabin classes, in-flight dining, entertainment and cargo services.

name: IndiGo
description: A major Indian airline known for its extensive domestic network and international operations.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A321neo and ATR 72-600 aircraft.
destinations: Destinations across India and international markets. The network and destination count can change.
history: Founded in 2006, IndiGo began scheduled operations that year and grew into one of India's largest passenger airlines.
services: Domestic and international flights, optional seat selection, food purchases, baggage options and connecting travel services.

name: Emirates
description: A Dubai-based international airline connecting passengers across a large global network.
fleet: Airbus A380, Airbus A350 and Boeing 777 aircraft.
destinations: Destinations across Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, the Middle East and the Pacific.
history: Established in 1985, Emirates began flights from Dubai and grew into a major international airline.
services: Multiple cabin classes, in-flight entertainment, dining and cargo services.

name: Qatar Airways
description: Qatar's flag carrier, operating international passenger services through its Doha hub.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A330, Airbus A350, Airbus A380, Boeing 777 and Boeing 787 aircraft.
destinations: International destinations across the Middle East, Asia, Europe, Africa, the Americas and Oceania.
history: Established in 1993, Qatar Airways began operations in 1994 and expanded its international network from Doha.
services: Multiple cabin classes, in-flight dining, entertainment, lounge access for eligible passengers and cargo services.

name: Etihad Airways
description: An Abu Dhabi-based airline serving destinations across several continents.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A350, Boeing 787 and other aircraft types used across its fleet.
destinations: Destinations across the Middle East, Asia, Europe, Africa, Australia and the Americas.
history: Founded in 2003, Etihad Airways began commercial operations later that year and developed Abu Dhabi into an international aviation hub.
services: Multiple cabin classes, in-flight dining, entertainment, loyalty rewards and cargo services.

name: Singapore Airlines
description: Singapore's flag carrier, known for its international passenger network and cabin services.
fleet: Airbus A350, Airbus A380, Boeing 737 and Boeing 777/787 family aircraft, depending on operating division.
destinations: Destinations across Asia, Europe, Australia, Africa and the Americas.
history: Singapore Airlines was formed in 1972 following the separation of Malaysia-Singapore Airlines into separate national carriers.
services: Multiple cabin classes, in-flight dining, entertainment and loyalty programmes.

name: Japan Airlines
description: A major Japanese airline providing domestic and international passenger services.
fleet: Airbus A350, Boeing 737, Boeing 767, Boeing 777, Boeing 787 and regional aircraft across the JAL Group.
destinations: Domestic destinations throughout Japan and international routes across Asia, Europe, North America and other regions.
history: Established in 1951, Japan Airlines began operations in the post-war period and grew into one of Japan's major international carriers.
services: Domestic and international flights, multiple cabin classes, in-flight meals, entertainment and loyalty rewards.

name: Lufthansa
description: A major German airline linking European cities with destinations around the world.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A330, Airbus A340, Airbus A350, Airbus A380 and Boeing 747/787 family aircraft.
destinations: European and intercontinental destinations across the Americas, Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
history: The present Lufthansa was founded in 1953 and began flight operations in 1955. It later expanded its international network and airline group.
services: Multiple cabin classes, lounges for eligible travellers, in-flight dining, entertainment and cargo services.

name: British Airways
description: A major British airline operating domestic, European and long-haul international services.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A350, Airbus A380, Boeing 777 and Boeing 787 aircraft.
destinations: Destinations across Europe, North America, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and other regions.
history: British Airways was created in 1974 following the merger of BOAC and BEA.
services: Multiple cabin classes, in-flight dining, entertainment and loyalty rewards.

name: Air France
description: France's flag carrier, serving domestic, European and intercontinental destinations.
fleet: Airbus A220, Airbus A320 family, Airbus A330, Airbus A350, Boeing 777 and Boeing 787 aircraft.
destinations: Destinations across Europe, Africa, Asia, the Americas and the Middle East.
history: Founded in 1933 through the merger of several French aviation companies, Air France developed into a major international airline.
services: Multiple cabin classes, in-flight dining, entertainment, loyalty rewards and cargo services.

name: American Airlines
description: A major United States airline with an extensive domestic and international route network.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A321 family, Boeing 737, Boeing 777 and Boeing 787 aircraft.
destinations: Destinations across the United States and international markets, with partner-airline connections expanding travel options.
history: American Airlines began operating under its present name in 1936 after the consolidation of several smaller aviation businesses.
services: Domestic and international flights, premium cabins on selected routes, in-flight entertainment, loyalty rewards and cargo services.

name: Air New Zealand
description: New Zealand's flag carrier, linking the country with domestic and international destinations.
fleet: Airbus A320 family, Airbus A321neo, Boeing 787, Boeing 777, ATR 72-600 and De Havilland Canada Q300 aircraft.
destinations: Domestic destinations across New Zealand and international destinations in Australia, the Pacific, Asia and North America.
history: Established in 1940 as Tasman Empire Airways Limited, the airline later became Air New Zealand and expanded its services.
services: Domestic and international flights, multiple cabin classes on selected aircraft, in-flight dining, entertainment, loyalty rewards and cargo services.
